visitors.name: Robert Pope II
visitors.title: Undergraduate Cybersecurity Researcher
visitors.description: Full-time, on-site in Starkville, Mississippi. Project trained me to address cybersecurity challenges in shared spectrum management such as detecting interference, anomalous signals, and ensuring data privacy. I developed and evaluated machine learning algorithms capable of identifying overlapping RF signals, applied homomorphic encryption to preserve user privacy, and conducted real-world experiments using software-defined radios to validate solutions with real RF data. We saw an overall increase of 80% efficiency in securing signals, with model accuracy averaging about 81.2% in testing.

visitors.name: Tetevi Wilson
visitors.title: Research Intern
visitors.description: Internship, on-site in Starkville, Mississippi. Researched Differential Privacy (DP) and Federated Learning (FL) for secure wireless spectrum sharing, focusing on spectrogram-based CNNs in PyTorch. Built and evaluated DP-only and DP+FL models using Opacus, analyzing accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to assess privacy tradeoffs in a ResNet-50 architecture. Parsed and visualized training logs using TensorBoard and automated CSV extraction to support experiment tracking and a research poster presentation.
visitors.research: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Network Security Implementation
